title: Quentin and the Summer
premise: Yara Amberdale, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter scraping by on a stalled novel and a part-time job, dreads her family's centennial reunion on Gullwrack Island, where her successful ex-fiancé and her disapproving aunt will be watching. To survive the weekend, she hires Quentin Vale, a quiet stranger she meets at a ferry dock, to pose as her boyfriend, never guessing he is the anonymous ghostwriter behind her favorite novelist's recent books—and the man quietly deciding whether to claim his own name at last. As the fake relationship turns real by dessert and real by dawn, Yara must confront the family memory she buried: the night her father's fishing boat went down and she survived by staying silent. When Quentin's identity is exposed at the reunion's final toast and Yara's aunt threatens to reveal the truth about her father, both must choose between the safe invisibility that saved them and the risky visibility of being truly seen. The story ends with Quentin publicly crediting his own work and Yara publishing her novel under her real name, the two of them keeping the lighthouse lit together as the summer closes.
about_author: Orsen Nystrom is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloging lighthouse logs along the northern coast before turning to fiction. Known for romances steeped in salt air, family secrets, and second chances, Nystrom writes from a restored keeper's cottage with an unreliable view of the sea.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Stuck in a dead-end job and a stalled manuscript, Yara receives her aunt's summons to the Amberdale centennial reunion, where her ex-fiancé will attend with his new wife. On the ferry dock she overhears a stranger calmly declining a job. Emotional beat: restless dread meeting an unexpected spark of curiosity.

chapters.title: A Stranger Willing to Lie
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She impulsively offers Quentin Vale money to pose as her boyfriend for the reunion weekend. He hesitates, then agrees, with one condition: no questions about his past. Emotional beat: the thrill and guilt of hiring intimacy, and the first crack in Yara's careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. On the crossing to Gullwrack, Yara and Quentin negotiate their backstory—how they met, why she left the city, what he does. Quentin is suspiciously fluent at inventing lives. Emotional beat: playful complicity shadowed by the sense that he's rehearsed this escape before.

chapters.title: The Amberdale House
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Arrival at the weathered family house; her aunt Marguerite's icy appraisal of Quentin, her ex-fiancé Daniel's smug greeting, and her grandmother's lighthouse looming over the cliffs. Emotional beat: Yara shrinks into the role her family wrote for her, with Quentin unexpectedly holding the door open.

chapters.title: First Performance
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the welcome dinner, Quentin plays the devoted boyfriend so convincingly that Yara almost believes it. He notices how her family talks over her, and how she apologizes for existing. Emotional beat: Quentin's protective anger, and his own discomfort at how easily he wears a false name.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Escaping the reunion, Yara takes Quentin to the lighthouse and tells the official story of her father's drowning—careful, polished, false. Quentin listens like it matters. Emotional beat: the first true intimacy, built on a lie she doesn't yet know he can see through.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the reunion banquet, Daniel needles Yara publicly; Quentin's hand finds hers under the table and neither lets go. Marguerite announces a family toast that will honor the drowned. Emotional beat: the fake relationship tipping into something neither of them planned, witnessed by a room full of critics.

chapters.title: What Quentin Writes at Night
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Unable to sleep, Quentin drafts pages in a notebook—revealing to the reader, not Yara, that he is the anonymous ghostwriter behind celebrated novelist E. R. Marsh's recent bestsellers, and that he is being pressured to sign a contract that erases him permanently. Emotional beat: the ache of a man famous for being no one.

chapters.title: The Storm Cellar
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A summer storm traps the reunion indoors; Yara and Quentin take shelter in the old storm cellar, where she finds her father's last letter, unopened for twenty years. Emotional beat: terror of the past surfacing, softened by Quentin's steady presence beside her in the dark.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She finally reads the letter: her father knew the boat was unsafe and went out anyway to pay for her schooling. Yara's survival—and her silence about the letter—is the family's open wound. Emotional beat: guilt reframed; the price of survival made explicit for the first time.

chapters.title: Midsummer Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. On the beach at midnight, Yara tells Quentin the truth about the letter; Quentin nearly tells her his own secret and can't. They kiss. Emotional beat: two people offering half-honesties and receiving whole tenderness, the imbalance quietly loaded.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Leverage
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Marguerite corners Yara: she knows about the letter, knows Yara hid it, and will use it to claim the lighthouse property unless Yara signs away her inheritance and stays out of the family's way. Emotional beat: the reunion's cruelty sharpening into real stakes.

chapters.title: The Ghostwriter's Contract
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin's agent calls: E. R. Marsh's publisher wants Quentin to sign away all rights permanently in exchange for money that would solve every problem he has. Emotional beat: the career that saved everything offered as a cage, with Yara's face suddenly complicating the math.

chapters.title: Reading Aloud
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara shares her unfinished novel with Quentin—the first person besides her grandmother to hear it. His feedback is generous and precise, and Yara realizes he understands craft at a professional level. Emotional beat: creative intimacy, and the first flicker of Yara's suspicion about who Quentin really is.

chapters.title: The Name on the Spine
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the family library, Yara finds a signed advance copy of the newest E. R. Marsh novel—inscribed with a phrase she heard Quentin say word for word. Emotional beat: betrayal and recognition colliding; the man she's falling for has been a stranger all along.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Cliffs
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Yara demands the truth; Quentin admits everything—his name, his erasure, the contract. Yara, stung by the parallel to her own silence, says the unforgivable: that he's exactly like her, hiding. Emotional beat: the midpoint rupture, both of them weaponizing honesty.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the reunion's final night, Marguerite rises to toast the drowned and publicly exposes Yara's hidden letter, framing her silence as betrayal. Daniel smirks; the family turns. Emotional beat: Yara's worst fear realized—seen, finally, in the cruelest light.

chapters.title: Quentin Stands Up
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin interrupts the toast and publicly claims his own name, announcing he is the author behind E. R. Marsh and that he'd rather be a real, flawed person than a profitable ghost. Emotional beat: the climax's first half—Quentin choosing visibility at the cost of the career that saved him.

chapters.title: What Yara Says
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Shaken by Quentin's courage, Yara takes the floor: she reads her father's letter aloud and tells the truth of her survival, then declares she will keep the lighthouse and finish her novel under her own name. Emotional beat: the second half of the climax—Yara choosing to be seen, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: After the Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The reunion scatters; Marguerite's hold breaks as the family rallies around the truth. Quentin and Yara, raw and apart, each confront what they gave up and whether love is worth the exposure. Emotional beat: the quiet, aching aftermath where both must decide alone.

chapters.title: The Manuscript and the Man
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin arrives at the lighthouse with his signed resignation from the ghostwriting deal and a proposal: they finish their books side by side. Yara, who nearly let pride keep her invisible, opens the door. Emotional beat: reconciliation earned, not given—two writers choosing their own names and each other.

chapters.title: Keeping the Light
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue. One year later: Yara's novel is published under Yara Amberdale; Quentin's first book under his own name sits beside it in the lighthouse bookshop. They light the lamp together for the season's first dark. Emotional beat: resolution—identity claimed, memory honored, and a love that survives being fully seen.
